name: Turkiye
headline: Turkiye: +3.7% growth in 2025, 34.9% inflation, debt 24% of GDP
sections: Turkiye is a $1.60 trillion economy (2025), the world's 17th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +3.7% in 2025, close to the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $45K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 16.8% of GDP (2024).

Consumer prices rose 34.9% in 2025, well above typical central bank targets, down from 72.3% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 8.3% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 16.0% (2025).
Gross government debt is 24% of GDP (2025), a low level that has fallen from 38% in 2020. The general government balance is −2.8% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is −1.9% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 50% of GDP (2025), a relatively closed economy. Net FDI inflows were 0.8% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 25% of GDP by 2031, broadly stable from today's level. Life expectancy is 77.4 years (2024). Population: 85.8 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
